rationale: The verified paper passage states an algorithm-specific exact split between scheme and perturbation errors, then separate local asymptotic orders and a stability-conditional global order. The Lean proposition instead states a generic Euclidean triangle inequality for arbitrary finite real vectors. Surface reuse of the words schemeError and perturbationError and of an addition operation supplies no semantic linkage to the Runge-Kutta method. Neither statement semantically implies the other under their actual binders and meanings, so the result is not-faithful-different. The paper's perturbation-sign ambiguity does not require adjudication here because the Lean target omits the entire perturbation model and the mismatch is decisive independently of that sign.
